clue.text: Left out of divorce payments, needing credit instead makes for bitterness

indicators.note: the word for left is to come out of the payments word, so its letter is removed
the credit letters go in where the left letter was, replacing it

parts.note: alimony is the money paid to a former spouse after divorce
CR is the accounting abbreviation for credit

explanation.surface: Someone stung by a divorce settlement, short of cash and borrowing, is left feeling bitter.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Left out of' removes L from ALIMONY and 'instead' puts CR in its place.
explanation.definitionFit: Acrimony is harsh, resentful feeling between people, a close synonym of bitterness.

clue.text: College that'll charge accepting first of international students on programme that's sure to have an impact

indicators.note: in a down clue one piece written on top of another comes before it
college and charged-particle words together take in the next letters, which sit between them

parts.note: COLL is an abbreviation for college
an ion is a particle that carries an electric charge

indicators.note: only the opening letter of the next word is used

parts.note: S is a short form for students, as in plural abbreviations
a course is a programme of study

explanation.surface: A college fee policy for overseas students looks like it is heading for trouble.
explanation.walkthrough: 'that'll charge' is an ion, a charged particle; 'accepting' puts the two student letters into the college-and-ion pair, and 'on' stacks the first word above the second in a down entry.
explanation.definitionFit: A collision course is a path or plan that will inevitably end in a crash or confrontation.

clue.text: He plays up-and-coming talented gentleman detective

indicators.note: in a down clue, coming up means the letters read from bottom to top, so they are reversed

parts.note: able means talented or capable
Sir is the title of a knighted gentleman
DI is a Detective Inspector

explanation.surface: A rising star portrays a gifted, gentlemanly sleuth.
explanation.walkthrough: 'up-and-coming' reverses ABLE + SIR + DI, reading up the column. Idris Elba played the detective DCI John Luther in the BBC series Luther.
explanation.definitionFit: Idris Elba is an actor, someone who plays roles, so 'He plays' describes him.

clue.text: Best garden party?

definitions.meaning: to best someone is to beat or surpass them
a party held outdoors is an '...', do being an informal word for a party

explanation.surface: A boast about the finest outdoor social event.
explanation.definitionFit: To outdo is to surpass, the verb sense of best; split as OUT DO it is an outside party, a garden party being one example.

clue.text: Distortion affecting my radar beam

indicators.note: distortion twists the shape of something, so these letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Interference is messing up the beam of my radar.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Distortion affecting' rearranges the letters of MY RADAR. 'Beam' looks like part of the radar picture but is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: A yardarm is the horizontal spar, or beam, on a ship's mast from which a sail is hung.

clue.text: Cut and run inside, having run out of clothes

indicators.note: the run letter goes inside the meat word

parts.note: a steak is a cut of meat
R is the cricket abbreviation for run

explanation.surface: Instructions for a quick escape: slash, flee, and get indoors after leaving your clothes behind.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Cut and run' looks like the idiom for fleeing, but 'Cut' is a steak. 'inside' puts R into STEAK.
explanation.definitionFit: To streak is to run naked in public, so it is to run without any clothes on.

clue.text: Trace where takings go in accounts subject to turnover

indicators.note: the till phrase goes inside the reversed accounts letters
turned over, the letters of the accounts word read the other way

parts.note: ACS is an abbreviation for accounts
a shop's takings go 'in till', into the cash register

explanation.surface: An auditor tracking where a shop's money goes in books affected by turnover.
explanation.walkthrough: 'subject to turnover' reverses ACS to SCA, and 'in' puts IN TILL inside it. 'Turnover' looks like business revenue but is the reversal signal.
explanation.definitionFit: A scintilla is a tiny amount, the merest trace or hint of something.

clue.text: Lift to get to ground level, according to announcement

indicators.note: the word is spoken aloud, so its sound gives the answer's spelling

parts.note: to raze a building is to bring it down to ground level

explanation.surface: An elevator instruction on how to reach the ground floor, as heard over a tannoy.
explanation.walkthrough: RAZE and RAISE sound alike but mean opposites, which is the joke of the clue.
explanation.definitionFit: To raise something is to lift it up.

clue.text: Mate carnally in a teeming lunchtime tube?

indicators.note: teeming means swarming and seething, so these letters are churned into a new order

explanation.surface: A saucy scene of couples pairing off in a crowded Tube carriage at lunchtime.
explanation.walkthrough: 'teeming' signals an anagram of MATE CARNALLY IN A. 'Tube' looks like the London Underground but is the digestive tract.
explanation.definitionFit: The alimentary canal is the digestive passage from mouth to anus, the tube food travels through after lunch.

clue.text: Worry about contents of aloo gobi portion?

indicators.note: the worry word goes around the next letters

parts.note: to fret is to worry

indicators.note: the contents are the inner letters, dropping the first and last

explanation.surface: Fretting over what is in an Indian potato and cauliflower dish.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about' wraps the worry word round the inner letters of 'aloo'. Aloo gobi is a potato (aloo) and cauliflower (gobi) curry, so 'gobi portion' is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Gobi is cauliflower, and a floret is one of the small flowering clusters that make up a cauliflower head.

clue.text: Dressed in shirt, I get running with this!

indicators.note: to dress something is to arrange or prepare it, so these letters are set out anew

explanation.surface: Someone who puts on a shirt before going out for a jog.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Dressed' rearranges IN SHIRT I. 'Running' suggests jogging, but here it is a runny nose.
explanation.definitionFit: Rhinitis is inflammation of the nasal lining, which makes the nose run.

clue.text: Did state back meagre half-hearted aid initially for migrants?

indicators.note: back means the stated word is read backwards

parts.note: said means stated

indicators.note: the heart of the meagre word is a pair of letters, and half of that pair is dropped

parts.note: poor means meagre or scanty

indicators.note: only the opening letter of the following word is used

explanation.surface: A complaint that aid for migrants has been cut to a meagre and grudging level.
explanation.walkthrough: 'back' reverses SAID to DIAS; 'half-hearted' drops one O of POOR's middle OO, leaving POR; 'initially' takes A from 'aid'.
explanation.definitionFit: A diaspora is a people scattered away from their homeland, so its members are migrants; the question mark marks that looser fit.

clue.text: Sea, informally styled

definitions.meaning: 'the Med' is the casual name for the Mediterranean Sea
designed around a particular style or idea

explanation.surface: A sea described in casual, fashionable terms.
explanation.definitionFit: A themed party or restaurant is styled on one idea; split as THE MED it is the Mediterranean in casual speech.

clue.text: Victoria's fourth, and her chap's third bottle

indicators.note: a fourth of the eight-letter queen's name is its opening two letters, a quarter of it
only a third of the six-letter name survives, so its last four letters are cut away

parts.note: Prince Albert was Queen Victoria's husband

explanation.surface: A recipe of royal ingredients: some Victoria, a bit of Albert, and a bottle to put them in.
explanation.walkthrough: 'fourth' means a quarter of the eight letters of Victoria, her first two; 'third' keeps the first third of ALBERT, Victoria's husband, cutting BERT.
explanation.definitionFit: A vial is a small glass container, a little bottle for medicine or perfume.

clue.text: Among guilty parties losing appeal with irritated snarl

indicators.note: losing means the appeal word is taken out of the longer word

parts.note: to be complicit is to be one of those involved in wrongdoing
IT is an old informal word for sex appeal
ate is used for annoyed, as in 'what's eating you?'

explanation.surface: Guilty people, no longer charming, growl angrily at one another.
explanation.walkthrough: 'losing' removes IT from COMPLICIT, leaving COMPLIC. 'Snarl' looks like a growl but is the verb meaning to tangle.
explanation.definitionFit: To snarl something is to tangle it up, and to complicate is to make it tangled and involved.

clue.text: Murmuring softly together, perhaps, wrapping son's bottom and protecting

parts.note: co- is the prefix meaning together, as in co-operate

indicators.note: the cooing word wraps around the next letter

parts.note: cooing is the soft murmuring sound of doves and lovers

indicators.note: in a down clue the bottom of a word is its last letter

explanation.surface: Lovers whispering sweet nothings while tucking a baby son in to keep him safe.
explanation.walkthrough: 'perhaps' flags CO-COOING, murmuring together, as an invented word; 'wrapping' puts N, the bottom of 'son', inside it.
explanation.definitionFit: Cocooning is wrapping something up to shield it, as a cocoon protects a pupa.

clue.text: Lips with a drawback for love-making?

definitions.meaning: a ... is the double curve of the upper lip
... is the bow the love god draws back to fire arrows that make people fall in love

explanation.surface: A complaint that someone's mouth is a turn-off in romance.
explanation.definitionFit: The name of the upper-lip curve comes from its likeness to the archer's weapon held by the Roman god of love.

clue.text: A nationalist manoeuvre involving Republican on American continent

indicators.note: the manoeuvre word takes in the Republican letter

parts.note: a tactic is a manoeuvre

explanation.surface: A political story: a nationalist ploy that drags in a Republican on American soil.
explanation.walkthrough: 'involving' puts R inside TACTIC to make TARCTIC.
explanation.definitionFit: Antarctica is the ice-covered continent around the South Pole.

clue.text: Disastrous bin fire, put simply

indicators.note: a disastrous event leaves things wrecked and scattered, so the letters are jumbled

explanation.surface: A short account of a rubbish bin going up in flames.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Disastrous' rearranges BIN FIRE.
explanation.definitionFit: In brief means briefly or in a few words, the same as putting something simply.

clue.text: A king's emolument

parts.note: 'a' can mean per, as in two pounds a head
K is the chess abbreviation for king

explanation.surface: A monarch's salary or allowance.
explanation.walkthrough: 'A' stands for PER, as in 'ten miles a day'; the 's of king's is read as 'has' to link the pieces.
explanation.definitionFit: A perk is an extra benefit that comes with a job, a fringe emolument.

clue.text: Our cousin's a singer and a half

parts.note: Bono is the lead singer of the Irish band U2

indicators.note: only half of that further copy, its opening two letters, is kept

parts.note: 'and' adds a further copy of that singer's name

explanation.surface: Boasting that a relative is a singer and then some.
explanation.walkthrough: BO is half of BONO. 'Our cousin' works because bonobos are great apes, close relatives of humans.
explanation.definitionFit: The bonobo is an ape closely related to humans, a cousin in evolutionary terms.

clue.text: Tender assassin?

definitions.meaning: to tender is to ..., as in tendering a bid
to 'off' someone is slang for kill

explanation.definitionFit: Tender as a verb means to put forward, as an offer does; the question mark marks the invented killer sense.

clue.text: Drunken date getting stuck into beer where the floor may start to sway!

definitions.text: where the floor may start to sway!

indicators.note: the shuffled letters go inside the beer word

parts.note: bock is a strong German beer

indicators.note: a drunken person staggers about, so these letters are scrambled

explanation.surface: A tipsy evening out where the beer flows and the dance floor starts to wobble.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Drunken' scrambles 'date' and 'getting stuck into' puts the result inside a German beer. The swaying floor is a ship's, not a pub's.
explanation.definitionFit: A boat deck is the deck of a ship carrying the lifeboats, a floor that sways with the sea.

clue.text: Turn bank payment into beer

indicators.note: the payment letters go into the beer word

parts.note: ale is a type of beer
DD is a direct debit, a payment made through a bank

explanation.surface: Instructions for converting a bank transfer into a pint.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Turn' looks like an instruction but is the definition: eggs that turn go bad. 'into' puts the direct-debit letters inside the beer.
explanation.definitionFit: Eggs that turn go rotten, which is what addle means; it can also mean to confuse.

clue.text: Group of established artists in squabble over street art

parts.note: G stands for group, as in G7
RA is the Royal Academy, or a Royal Academician, an established artist

indicators.note: turned over, the squabble word reads backwards

parts.note: a tiff is a minor squabble
i' is a poetic shortening of in, so it gives the single letter

explanation.surface: Members of the art establishment quarrel about whether street art counts.
explanation.walkthrough: 'over' reverses TIFF to FFIT. The poetic contraction i' for 'in' gives the last I.
explanation.definitionFit: Graffiti is writing or drawing sprayed or scratched on public walls, the classic form of street art.

clue.text: Get out of bed and show up

definitions.meaning: read as ..., to take away from a bunk, which is a bed
to expose a claim as false, to show it up

explanation.surface: Rising in the morning and then putting in an appearance.
explanation.definitionFit: To debunk is to expose as false; split as DE-BUNK it whimsically means leaving one's bunk bed.

clue.text: Socialist paper that — according to Spooner — doesn't get Keir Starmer?

definitions.meaning: a left-wing newspaper, red meaning socialist and rag a newspaper

definitions.text: that — according to Spooner — doesn't get Keir Starmer?
definitions.meaning: a ... to a bull enrages it, so it does not get a 'steer calmer', which Spooner would say as Keir Starmer

explanation.surface: A left-wing newspaper that doesn't understand the Labour leader Keir Starmer.
explanation.walkthrough: The Spoonerism is in the clue: swapping the opening sounds of 'steer calmer' gives Keir Starmer. A red rag to a bull makes it angrier, never calmer.
explanation.definitionFit: Red means socialist and rag is slang for a newspaper; the second sense comes from the saying 'like a red rag to a bull'.

clue.text: Choice to miss end of film

indicators.note: the film title loses its final letter

parts.note: Free Willy is a 1993 film about a captive killer whale

explanation.surface: Deciding whether or not to skip the end of a movie.
explanation.definitionFit: Free will is the power of choosing for oneself, the capacity behind any choice.
